Panjrapur treatment-plant operating data span April 1995 through March 2011; the estimated forest-cover change rate is -0.0088 percent per year and its modeled observed-system burden is INR 3.73 million per year in 2010-2011 prices.
TERI reports an annual forest-cover change rate of -0.0088 percent averaged over 1994-2007.
TERI reports INR 64.96 per cubic metre of treated water per hectare per year and INR 3.73 million per year in deforestation-induced Panjrapur treatment costs.

Normalize only the study-estimated INR 3.73 million annual Panjrapur burden in 2010-2011 prices; do not separately score elasticities or water-loss channels.

source_locators.depletion: UN World Water Development Report 2022 executive summary: global aggregated groundwater storage depletion at the beginning of this century is mostly estimated between 100 and 200 cubic kilometres per year, around 15 to 25 percent of withdrawals.

source_locators.agricultural_dependence: UN World Water Development Report 2022: agriculture accounts for about 69 to 70 percent of groundwater abstractions and groundwater serves 38 percent of irrigated land.
source_locators.demand_duration: UN World Water Development Report 2024 statistics: global freshwater demand has increased by just under one percent per year since the 1980s.
source_locators.irrigation_loss: FAO assessment: 40 percent or more of irrigation withdrawals are lost through conveyance leakage, deep percolation or surface runoff, while noting that some flows are recoverable.
source_locators.irrigation_food_system: FAO AQUASTAT: irrigated agriculture uses about 70 percent of freshwater withdrawals and produces about 40 percent of global food on 20 percent of cultivated land.
source_locators.irrigation_extent: FAO AQUASTAT irrigation-withdrawal assessment covers 167 countries and territories, including 118 with nationally sourced withdrawal information.

groundwater dependence treated as realized shortage

The page distinguishes later September fires and declarations from the August lightning-siege extent used by this receipt.
QuickFacts reports California land area of 155,858.33 square miles in 2020.

Surface infiltration fell from 28.5 centimetres per day in ungrazed controls to 7, 5 and 5 centimetres per day under low, moderate and high stocking density.
The field experiment compared soil compaction caused by cattle trampling and tractor use with uncompacted grassland and evaluated grass yield and quality.
First-cut grass-silage yield loss reached 19.0 percent under cattle trampling; the larger 37.7-percent tractor result is excluded.
By the third year, the experiment measured a 14.3-percent annual loss of grass dry-matter yield.

source_locators: Across 465 cities, districts or counties monitoring precipitation, mean acid-rain frequency was 10.3% in 2020.
The official thresholds are annual precipitation pH below 5.6 for acid rain, below 5.0 for relatively serious acid rain and below 4.5 for serious acid rain.
The acid-rain area was approximately 466,000 square kilometres, or 4.8% of China’s land area, 0.2 percentage point below 2019.
The assessment uses annual precipitation pH and ambient SO2 from the China National Environmental Monitoring Network for 338 municipalities and prefecture-level cities and 1,436 air-quality stations.
Dose-response functions, material exposure inventories and maintenance or replacement prices produce an estimated RMB 32.165 billion in acid-deposition material loss for 2013.
The estimate equals 0.057% of GDP and 3.4% of national environmental-pollution-control investment in 2013; it is a modeled loss rather than audited expenditure.
The 2003 national bulletin reports acid-rain monitoring across 487 cities and counties.
Acid rain occurred in 265 monitored jurisdictions, while 182 had annual mean precipitation pH at or below 5.6.
The bulletin provides the first year used in this receipt’s documented national monitoring span; the span is not interpreted as continuous station-level completeness.

source_locators: Whiskey Creek Shellfish Hatchery observed direct acidification impacts beginning in 2007, with larval culture reduced by 75 percent or more.
Researchers and hatchery operators linked the failures to summer upwelling of deep acidified water and developed water-chemistry management practices.
The report bounds the event to oyster larvae at the Netarts Bay hatchery rather than inferring biological failure from regional chemistry alone.
High larval mortality began in July 2007 and persisted through the end of the growing season in October; magnitude and duration were unprecedented in the hatchery's 30-year history.
Whiskey Creek produced about 2.5 billion eyed larvae in 2008, approximately 25 percent of a normal season, implying a documented normal level of about 10 billion.
Pacific coast hatcheries produced 40-60 billion eyed larvae annually and supported a USD 270 million-per-year shellfish industry.
Commercial hatcheries experienced unprecedented Pacific-oyster larval mortality beginning in 2007.
Whiskey Creek records showed a high correlation between inflowing aragonite saturation state and larval-group survival, linking increased carbon dioxide to the hatchery failures.
Commercial treatment and monitoring systems restored billions of additional larvae, while the reviewed minimum aragonite saturation threshold for viable larval groups was about 1.7.

transformations.formula: Normalize the documented at-least-75-percent Pacific-oyster larval-culture reduction while retaining the hatchery-specific aragonite threshold as paired chemistry evidence.
Divide 2.5 billion actual larvae by 0.25 to derive 10 billion normal production, then subtract actual output to obtain a 7.5-billion-larvae shortfall; do not monetize it.
Normalize the two documented affected production seasons, 2007 and 2008, rather than treating the entire later monitoring period as failure.
Normalize 50 percent, the lower end of the hatchery's documented 50-85 percent supply share of West Coast oyster operations.
0.35B + 0.30H + 0.20P + 0.15E; convert to 1-10 with 1 + 9 × composite and round to one decimal.

receipts.uncertainty: The 75 percent value is a lower bound on larval-culture reduction and is not a universal species threshold. Normal production is derived from the source statement that 2.5 billion was 25 percent of normal; the resulting 7.5-billion shortfall is an output estimate, not a dollar loss. The 1.7 aragonite saturation threshold is hatchery-, species-, life-stage- and method-specific. Bacterial disease was an early competing hypothesis, and multiple stressors can affect larvae; the receipt relies on the later paired chemistry and cohort evidence. The 50 percent supply share is the conservative end of the documented 50-85 percent range. The USD 270 million regional industry value remains unscored context.

source_locators: During austral summer 2008–2009 off southern Peru, Chrysaora plocamia exceeded 30 percent of catch weight in 5 percent of observed hauls.
Processing plants refused catches when jellyfish exceeded 40 percent by weight.
The study estimated more than US$200,000 of losses during 35 fishing days using observer bycatch rates and interviews with processing-factory employees.
The report preserves the Peru observer result that jellyfish exceeded 10 percent of catch weight in 10 percent of hauls and exceeded 30 percent in 5 percent of hauls.
Catches above the 40-percent rejection threshold were refused 13 times at Ilo, with about 387 tonnes discarded.
The bounded 35-day economic loss was approximately US$200,000; seasonal and national extrapolations are excluded from scoring.

transformations.formula: Normalize the documented greater-than-30-percent jellyfish share of catch weight; retain that this occurred in 5 percent of hauls and do not convert it to water-column density.
Normalize the source-reported lower-bound US$200,000 loss over the observed 35 fishing days; exclude seasonal and national extrapolations.
Normalize 35 observed fishing days and 13 catch-rejection events; retain the 387-tonne discard as unconverted burden context.
0.35B + 0.30H + 0.20P + 0.15E; convert to 1-10 with 1 + 9 × composite and round to one decimal.

receipts.uncertainty: Catch-share observations are a fishery-dependent relative-biomass indicator, not an individuals-per-cubic-metre water-column survey. Loss estimates combine observer records with factory interviews and are specific to fishing and processing practices at the time. The source reports values as thresholds or approximate lower bounds. Seasonal, national and climate-linked extrapolations remain unscored, and a single regional episode does not establish a global upward trend in jellyfish blooms.

source_locators: The assessment defines Tongass old-growth sawtimber as over 150 years old while noting that the full complement of old-growth features may not occur until about 250 years.
It reports 405,000 acres of productive old growth harvested from 1954–1995 and estimates another 45,000 acres from 1909–1954, for 450,000 acres total.
The assessment reports about 5.6 million acres of productive forest and states that clearcut even-aged management was the predominant harvest method.
GAO states that the Tongass timber program had been based on harvesting old-growth trees since the early twentieth century and that the transition to young growth was announced in 2010.
Forest Service data reviewed by GAO show average annual timber-related expenditures of $12.5 million and revenues of $1.1 million from fiscal years 2005–2014.
The expenditure figure excludes road construction and maintenance; the receipt therefore does not add an estimated road cost.

transformations.formula: Normalize the Forest Service estimate of 450,000 productive old-growth acres harvested, preserving the inventory-based and volume-derived portions separately.
Calculate $12.5 million average annual expenditures - $1.1 million average annual revenues = $11.4 million from FY2005–2014; do not add unreported road costs.
Calculate 1995 - 1909 = 86 years for the cumulative old-growth harvest assessment.
Calculate 450,000 / 5,600,000 × 100 = 8.035714 percent within the Tongass productive-forest boundary.
0.35B + 0.30H + 0.20P + 0.15E; convert to 1-10 with 1 + 9 × composite and round to one decimal.

receipts.uncertainty: The 45,000-acre 1909–1954 quantity is estimated from reported saw-log volume and an assumed per-acre harvest volume, while the 405,000-acre 1954–1995 quantity is inventory-based. Productive forest is a timber-capability class and is not identical to the old-growth denominator in every ecological interpretation. The 2005–2014 fiscal figures cover the Tongass timber program during a period when GAO describes the program as historically old-growth-based, but the figures are not allocated sale-by-sale between old and young growth. Net public cost excludes road construction and maintenance and is an administrative fiscal burden, not an ecological valuation.

The January 26-28 storm produced 10-15 inches of rain along coastal ranges, widespread Sierra snowfall above 48 inches, debris flows, wind damage and flooding.
NCEI bounds the event from January 24-29 and attributes USD 1.3 billion in CPI-adjusted damage and two deaths to the California flooding and severe-weather disaster.

The event damaged homes, vehicles, businesses and infrastructure, washed out Highway 1 and caused extensive power outages.

Count January 24-29 inclusively as six disaster-event days while keeping the shorter high-IVT interval explicit.

source_snapshot.coverage_boundary: This snapshot operationalizes global crop-yield variability, agricultural input-intensity components, apparent demand, mass-based food import dependency, fertilizer output, cereal feed use, and FAOSTAT agricultural drained-organic-soil area and carbon-dioxide emissions. The wetland records cover cropland and grassland organic soils only; they are not global observations of every drained wetland, newly drained area, peat fire or non-agricultural conversion. Country rows must not be summed with regional aggregates.

transformations.formula: Select the latest World total whose FAOSTAT flag is not I; retain 2023-2024 imputed repeats as excluded metadata.
Compare 2022 with the median of the complete 1990-1999 global annual inventory.
Normalize 2022 through median, 75th, 90th and 97.5th percentiles of 30 complete annual values from 1990-2019.
Calculate compound annual change from 2017 to 2022 without extrapolating beyond the inventory.

receipts.uncertainty: FAOSTAT flags combine official, estimated, imputed, and aggregate values. World and regional records inherit reporting and estimation uncertainty. Fertilizer product tonnes are not nutrient tonnes. Food import dependency depends on food-balance conventions, stock variation, re-exports, commodity aggregation, and mass rather than calorie weighting.
